rules.recovers: nearby calls misread as far jumps, which would glue a neighbouring function into the caller
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits bl as a jump only when the target is beyond the range of `b`; the shortest far jump in five ROMs is 1,960 bytes
rules.summary: a bl closer than farJump.minDistance to its target (the far-jump idiom fails) is a call

rules.recovers: pools and tables that would be free bytes for the gap scan to misread as functions
rules.restsOn: agbcc emits a function's literal pool and switch tables right after its code, separated only by alignment
rules.summary: the extent is the code plus the pools and tables right after it; claim those pools and every table

rules.recovers: functions proposed inside another function's unreached branch arms or alignment padding
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run, so the few bytes inside it the walk never reached are still its own
rules.summary: a dense function's free bytes inside its extent are claimed as dead code

rules.recovers: far pool words that the gap scan would misread as code or as the start of a function
rules.restsOn: a word loaded with `ldr rd, [pc, #imm]` is data wherever it sits; hand-written code shares pools across functions
rules.summary: pool words loaded from outside the extent are claimed as pool unless already claimed

rules.recovers: heap, OAM and map routines in ARM that no accepted code refers to
rules.restsOn: hand-written ARM keeps literal pools before its code and dispatches through branch tables, and is entered through RAM copies or computed jumps
rules.summary: an ARM function at the cursor or up to armFrontPoolWords words ahead of its own pools and tables, unreached by any reference

rules.recovers: functions reached only through computed addresses or not at all (dead code, callbacks named in data the harvest missed)
rules.restsOn: compiled functions are laid out back to back, so an unreferenced one starts where the previous one ends, give or take alignment
rules.summary: a valid Thumb reading at the cursor, first word nonzero, extent inside [gap start, end), chained forward from the gap start

rules.recovers: SoundMainRAM and other mixers on all five tuning ROMs
rules.restsOn: hand-written mixers keep ARM blocks and tables inside a Thumb function, so their extent has holes and their paths may not balance the stack
rules.summary: a gap's head reads as a function failing at most density or stack balance, with at least gapScan.minInsns instructions, its code inside the gap

rules.recovers: mixers and table-carrying functions in the middle of a gap, after the forward chain has taken the functions before them
rules.restsOn: compiled and hand-written code tiles the ROM: a reading that ends where the next function starts is that hole's function, dense or not
rules.summary: the hole head at a forward-chain cursor is accepted when it ends within fillSlack of the gap end or is anchored at its end

rules.recovers: the call graph below every accepted function
rules.restsOn: a bl (or a bx after mov lr, pc) that settles as a call enters a function
rules.summary: the targets of the calls of an accepted function are functions

rules.recovers: data and text decoded as code
rules.restsOn: every path of a compiled function decodes until it returns or jumps away
rules.summary: the walk from the entry decodes at least one instruction and hits no decode error

rules.recovers: data decoded as code, whose walk skips over bytes it never reaches
rules.restsOn: a compiled function is one contiguous run of code, pools and tables
rules.summary: holes inside the extent stay within max(minHoles, extent >> holeShift)
